concern: Urdu "اور نہریں اور راہیں بنا دیں" (and made rivers and paths) - دیں is the past-tense verb ("made/gave", fem. plural agreeing with نہریں اور راہیں), same construction as the owner's Q21 ruling (45:17): writing it "din" makes it read as "day" (دن). Should be "dein" per ADR 0005 R2/Q21.
suggestion: Aur is ne zameen mein pahaad gaad diye hain taake tumhein le kar hile na, aur nehren aur raahen bana dein taake tum manzil-e-maqsood ko pahuncho.

concern: ساعت (hour) is romanised "saaat" (three a's, no hyphen). The owner's explicit R5 ruling (canonical.tsv: saa'at -> saa-at) requires the hyphenated "saa-at", because plain "saat" would clash with "seven". Current spelling matches neither the old apostrophe form nor the ruled form.
suggestion: Agar logon ke gunaah par Allah Taala un ki giraft karta to roo-e-zameen par ek bhi jaandaar baaqi na rehta, lekin woh to unhein ek waqt-e-muqarrar tak dheel deta hai, jab un ka woh waqt aa jaata hai to woh ek saa-at na peechhe reh sakte hain aur na aage badh sakte hain.

concern: Urdu "اچھی اچھی چیزیں کھانے کو دیں" (gave you good things to eat) - دیں is the past-tense verb "gave" (fem. plural), same class as the owner's Q21 ruling: writing it "din" makes it read as "day". Should be "dein".
suggestion: Allah Taala ne tumhare liye tum mein se hi tumhari biwiyan paida kin aur tumhari biwiyon se tumhare liye tumhare bete aur pote paida kiye aur tumhein achchi achchi cheezen khaane ko dein. Kya phir bhi log baatil par imaan laayenge? Aur Allah Taala ki nematon ki na-shukri karenge?
